blocks.title: Reversible process
blocks.text: A reversible process is one which can be retraced in exactly reverse order without producing any change in the surroundings. In the reverse process the working substance passes through the same stages as in the direct process, but thermal and mechanical effects at each stage are exactly reversed: if heat is absorbed in the direct process it is given out in the reverse process, and if work is done by the substance in the direct process, work is done on the substance in the reverse process; hence the working substance is restored to its original conditions.

blocks.title: Cycle and reversible cycle
blocks.text: A succession of events which brings the system back to its initial condition is called a cycle. A reversible cycle is one in which all the changes are reversible.

Although no actual change is completely reversible, the processes of liquefaction and evaporation of a substance, performed slowly, are practically reversible. Similarly the slow compression of a gas in a cylinder is a reversible process, as the compression can be changed to expansion by slowly decreasing the pressure on the piston to reverse the operation.

blocks.title: Irreversible process
blocks.text: If a process cannot be retraced in the backward direction by reversing the controlling factors, it is an irreversible process. All changes which occur suddenly, or which involve friction or dissipation of energy through conduction, convection or radiation, are irreversible. An example of a highly irreversible process is an explosion.

blocks.caption: Reversible against irreversible
rows: cannot be retraced by reversing the controlling factors

blocks.prompt: Differentiate between reversible and irreversible processes (short question 6.5). Is the slow compression of a gas in a frictionless cylinder reversible, and why does friction spoil reversibility?
blocks.explanation: A reversible process can be run backwards through the same states with every heat and work exchange reversed and no trace left in the surroundings; an irreversible one cannot, and includes every sudden change and every process with friction or dissipation. Slow frictionless compression is practically reversible, since lowering the piston pressure slowly reverses it. Friction turns work into heat that cannot be turned back into the same work, so the surroundings are changed.

items: Reversible: can be retraced exactly with no change in the surroundings (slow liquefaction, evaporation, slow compression); a cycle returns the system to its initial state, a reversible cycle has all changes reversible. Irreversible: sudden changes, friction, dissipation by conduction, convection or radiation; an explosion.
